newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products--Diffs hold pat in wait of APIs.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products--Diffs hold pat in wait of APIs.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices rose Tuesday on technicals-driven stronger NYMEX values, but differentials were little changed despite the arrival of a Gulf Coast deadline for scheduling gasoline deliveries on the Colonial Pipeline.

Traders said differentials clung to their recent pattern of range-bound stability in all three hubs, although they added release late Tuesday of new stock data from the American Petroleum Institute might help break the stalemate.
A Reuters poll of traders showed expectations of moderate builds in gasoline and distillates.
July NYMEX heating oil rose 0.66 cent, to 52.60 cents a gallon, in early afternoon trade. July NYMEX gasoline climbed 0.67 cent, to 58.70 cents.
U.S. GULF
Differentials on grades of USG conventional unleaded gasoline eased a trace despite today's deadline for reserving space on the Colonial Pipeline for front-18th-cycle deliveries.
"The deadline is giving no help at all to the 'M' grades," one Gulf player said. "It's been kind of dead, although a few deals are getting done," he added.

Traders said USG "M2"-grade (9-lb Reid Vapor Pressure) conventional unleaded was sold for 3.60 cents below July NYMEX, while "M1"-grade (7.8 lb Reid Vapor Pressure) was offered for 3.15 cents below the screen.
But players said diffs widened about 0.15 cent on front-18th-cycle USG 54-grade jet fuel amid today's Colonial scheduling deadline, with parcels sold for 0.10 cent below the July screen.
Heating oil for front-18th-cycle delivery was sold for 2.25 cents below the July screen, traders said, stable with Monday differentials. Its Colonial scheduling deadline is not until Friday.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Differentials were steady in the Harbor, amid hopes among some traders that gasoline differentials might be set to start a firming trend.
"It feels like gasoline's been up so long that it might be ready for an uptick," said one trader.
Barge deals of prompt "M2" regular conventional unleaded were considered doable at 2.65 under July NYMEX, with "A2" regular reformulated pegged at between 0.50 and 0.25 cent under the July print.

Values on high octane material continued to hold their own, with "D2" 93-octane premium reformulated still pegged at more than 8.00 cents over July futures. Conventional "V2" 93-octane was heard offered at 5.50 cents over.
On the distillate front, values remained steady as well, though offers on "76-grade" heating oil were heard a touch firmer at 0.10 cent under July NYMEX.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were slightly lower amid a rise in NYMEX July futures and weaker rack, or wholesale, prices. In Group Three, prompt unleaded edged down a quarter cent to 4.25/4.50 cents in quiet trade. Any-month parcels were also softer at 2.80/3.00 cents.
In Chicago markets, prompt unleaded was pegged a quarter cent down at 3.25/3.50 cents over July NYMEX, with a 2.0 cent deal done for third cycle.
"The Merc is up and rack prices are discounted so players are trying to stay ahead," said one Group Three trader, noting the predominance of sellers Tuesday.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
